text: dsh-semantic-search 是面向 DSH 工作区的代码搜索插件，通过 Cordis bundle 注册 sema 工具，并在启动后建立或刷新持久索引。它按代码片段和符号边界切分文件，使用本地 lexical 向量与 BM25 混合排序，也可配置 OpenAI-compatible embedding 服务。用户可以搜索代码、查看索引状态、全量或增量重建索引，并通过文件监视保持索引更新。适合需要按自然语言或代码词查找项目实现的开发者；默认离线运行，无需额外服务配置。

dsh-semantic-search adds a sema tool for DSH code search. It indexes symbol-aware chunks and combines local vectors with BM25. Search by meaning or code terms, view index stats, and refresh fully or incrementally. Optional watching keeps the index current; the default provider works offline.

dsh-semantic-search 的功能「混合代码搜索」：在 sema 工具选择 search 并提供自然语言或代码查询，返回相关代码片段、符号、行号及排序分数。搜索融合向量相似度和 lexical BM25 候选。
dsh-semantic-search 的功能「刷新索引」：调用 sema 的 reindex 操作可增量更新索引，也可指定 full 重建或 path 处理单个文件。操作返回新增、更新、删除和未变更计数。
dsh-semantic-search 的功能「索引状态」：调用 sema 的 stats 操作可查看索引 provider、文件和片段数量、存储大小以及降级状态，便于确认索引是否可用。
dsh-semantic-search 的功能「自动维护索引」：插件启动时加载已有索引并按配置构建或刷新；启用 watcher 后，工作区文件变化会触发延迟刷新。
dsh-semantic-search 使用前须知：远程 embedding 会发送代码片段和查询到所配置的兼容服务；默认 lexical 模式离线运行。（见 src/engine/provider.ts:196-215）

Local semantic code search for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) — and any Node script.

> **中文文档：[README.zh.md](README.zh.md)**

dsh-semantic-search README · dsh-semantic-search：`sema` builds a **fragment-level index of a workspace**: source is tokenized by a
language-aware tokenizer (camel/snake/kebab splitting, CJK n-grams), chunked with
symbol-aware boundaries (functions/classes stay intact), and embedded into fixed
dimension vectors — **locally and dependency-free** by default (feature-hashed
lexical TF-IDF), or via any OpenAI-compatible embedding endpoint. Queries run a
**hybrid retrieval** (vector cosine + BM25, fused with reciprocal-rank fusion) over
the index, so meaning-based search works even when exact terms don't match.

dsh-semantic-search README · dsh-semantic-search：Ships as a dsh plugin bundle with one `sema` tool (`action=search`, `action=reindex`,
or `action=stats`) on the harness tool registry — plus a standalone `sema` CLI.

---

dsh-semantic-search README · Highlights：- **Works offline by default** — the built-in lexical provider needs no network,
  no model download, no API key. Use it as a fast BM25-plus code search.
- **Symbol-aware chunking** — boundaries from a conservative per-language table
  (16 languages) keep functions/classes intact; a missed boundary degrades to a
  plain chunk rather than breaking.
- **CJK-aware tokenizer** — n-gram tokenization (default bigrams) aligns Chinese
  queries and documents without a segmentation library; full-width punctuation is
  folded, not treated as a hard break.
- **Hybrid retrieval with RRF** — vector cosine + BM25 channels are fused by
  reciprocal-rank fusion, so a document found by one channel still ranks.
- **Graceful degradation** — if a configured remote provider is unreachable, the
  index falls back to the local lexical provider (configurable via `allowFallback`).
- **Incremental refresh + file watching** — `action=reindex` diffs by size+mtime,
  and an optional watcher keeps the index live.
- **Persistence** — the index is saved to `<root>/.sema` atomically (JSON metadata
  + binary vectors), with staleness detection when the provider/dimension chan

dsh-semantic-search README · dsh tool API：The plugin exposes a single `sema` tool. Set `action` to `search`, `stats`, or
`reindex`; for example, the argument objects are:

- Search: `{ "action": "search", "query": "find the retry loop" }`
- Stats: `{ "action": "stats" }`
- Full reindex: `{ "action": "reindex", "full": true }`

Search requires a `query` containing at least one non-whitespace character.
Missing, empty, or whitespace-only queries return a validation error.

dsh-semantic-search README · CLI usage：```sh
sema index                build the full index from the workspace
sema reindex [--full]     incremental refresh (or full rebuild with --full)
sema search <query...>    hybrid vector + BM25 search, prints top hits
sema stats [--json]       index health, provider, and sizing numbers

Global options:

dsh-semantic-search README · CLI usage：```
--root <dir>          workspace root (default: current directory)
--data-dir <dir>      index storage directory (default: <root>/.sema)
--provider <kind>     embedding provider: lexical | openai (default: lexical)
--dim <n>             embedding dimension (lexical default: 4096; openai 0 = auto)

dsh-semantic-search README · CLI exit codes：- `0` — success (including a search with zero hits and a `--version`/`--help` call).
- `1` — a runtime failure (config error, build/index/search error).
- `2` — a usage error: unknown command, unknown flag, or a missing/blank search query.

dsh-semantic-search README · Configuration：The plugin is configurable through the bundle row's `config` (see
`cordis.patch.yml` for an example), the CLI flags above, or defaults in code:

dsh-semantic-search README · Configuration：| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | cwd | workspace root to index |
| `dataDir` | `.sema` | index storage directory |
| `provider.kind` | `lexical` | `lexical` (offline) or `openai` |
| `provider.dimension` | `0` (lexical: 4096) | embedding dimension; `0` = auto-infer from the endpoint |
| `provider.baseUrl` | `https://api.openai.com/v1` | OpenAI-compatible endpoint root |
| `provider.apiKey` | empty | Explicit OpenAI API key; takes precedence over the environment and credentials store |
| `provider.model` | `text-embedding-3-small` | embedding model name |
| `provider.apiKeyEnv` | `SEMA_EMBEDDING_API_KEY` | Environment variable name and credentials-store reference |
| `allowFallback` | `true` | fall back to the lexical provider when a remote one fails |
| `include` / `ignore` | defaults | glob sets of files to index / skip |
| `maxLinesPerChunk` | `80` | hard chunk size upper bound |
| `nGram` | `2` | CJK n-gram size (`1` disables n-gramming) |
| `topK` | `20` | hits returned by default |
| `rrfK` | `60` | RRF fusion constant |
| `vectorK` | `300` | candidates per channel before fusion |
| `autosave` | `true` | p

dsh-semantic-search README · Configuration：OpenAI keys are selected in this order: `provider.apiKey`, the value of the
environment variable named by `provider.apiKeyEnv`, then the host credentials
store entry referenced by `provider.apiKeyEnv`. Store-backed keys are resolved
for each embedding operation so credential rotation takes effect without a
restart.
